newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst cites 1.7 bln dmk net debt in 97.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst cites 1.7 bln dmk net debt in 97.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Monday that it would incur some 1.7 billion marks in new net debt this year but that this figure would be offset by about one billion marks in debt payments.

"We will pick up about 1.7 billion marks in new net debt, but that is before repayment and we expect we will be able to repay about one billion marks of this this year," Hoechst chief financial officer Klaus-Juergen Schmieder told a conference call after the group released first quarter numbers.

Schmieder also said that Hoechst's 195 million marks in restructuring costs spent during the first quarter were related to a restructuring of the corporate research operation and the restructuring of Hoechst into a strategic management holding group.

Schmieder said that the group would usually expect to spend some 100 million marks per quarter on routine restructuring costs but that this year's total would be much higher, topping 500 million marks.
Hoechst last year announced plans to spin off its specialty chemicals unit to Swiss group Clariant AG and to purchase the outstanding stake it did not yet own in French group Roussel Uclaf.
